{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 70,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Global group manage check grants manage for VIEW permission",
      "body": "`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns true when the caller has either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). The no-argument `canManage()` is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` through `requireManage()`. A scope permission granting only `view` on `Groups` therefore allows creating or moving top-level groups, which is a privilege escalation. The check should require only `MANAGE`."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 123,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs",
      "body": "`GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is used to populate `UserModel.GROUPS` for user queries and counts. In V2, group instance resources are named by the realm group ID (`AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` returns `group.getId()`), but this method adds `groupResource.getId()` (the internal authorization resource ID) and also passes that value to `hasPermission()`, which expects a group ID and looks the resource up by name. The returned set therefore does not contain realm group IDs, so user search/count filtering by group permissions is wrong. It should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the returned set."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 121,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Instance resources are created without a resource type",
      "body": "`AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` creates instance resources for `Clients`, `Groups`, and `Users` but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` relies on `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` to find group instance resources. If instance resources have no type, they will not be returned, so group-scoped `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are not translated into group IDs for user queries/counts. The created resource should have its type set to `resourceType`."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 121,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Type-level group member permissions are not handled in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission",
      "body": "`GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` scans all resources of type `Groups`, which includes the type-level resource named `Groups` representing all groups. If a permission grants `view-members`/`manage-members` on all groups, this method either adds the type resource identifier (currently the wrong ID, but even with `getName()` it would be the literal string `Groups`) or cannot represent the grant as a set of group IDs. User count/search APIs that use this set will not reflect all-groups member permissions. The method needs explicit handling for the type-level resource."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 173,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Unsupported operations are thrown from V2 group permission management while existing code still calls them",
      "body": "`GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled()` (and `isPermissionsEnabled()`) throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. However `AdminPermissions.registerListener()` calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` on `GroupRemovedEvent` when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, and `GroupResource` management/permissions endpoints call `isPermissionsEnabled`/`setPermissionsEnabled`. If V1 and V2 fine-grained authz features are both enabled, group deletion or these endpoints can fail with an exception/500. For V2, cleanup/disable should be a no-op or the endpoints/listener must be guarded; throwing from lifecycle event handling is unsafe."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java",
      "line": 178,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Group-based user creation only checks V1 fine-grained authz feature",
      "body": "`UsersResource.canCreateGroupMembers()` returns false unless `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. This PR implements V2 fine-grained authz group scopes (`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`), and `AdminPermissions.evaluator()` may use V2 even when the V1 feature is disabled. In that configuration, callers with V2 `manage-members`/`manage-membership` group permissions cannot create users with initial group membership because the fallback permission check is skipped. The check should also consider V2/admin permissions enabled."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 238,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Possible NullPointerException in getScope for missing/unknown resource type",
      "body": "In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope()`, when the authorization schema is supported, the code calls `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes()` without checking whether `resourceType` is null or present in the map. An invalid or missing resource type will cause an NPE and HTTP 500 instead of a validation error. It should validate `resourceType` and throw a `ModelValidationException`."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 147,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Fallback to all-groups resource can NPE when type resource is unavailable",
      "body": "`GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can return null if the realm does not support the schema or the type resource has not been initialized. The method should null-check the fallback resource and return false instead of throwing NPE."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 334,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources",
      "body": "`AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName()` special-cases only `USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. For `Groups`, instance resources are stored with the group ID as the name and no display name is set, so this method returns `resource.getDisplayName()` (likely null) or the raw ID instead of a useful group name/path, and it does not return a label for the all-groups type resource. This can degrade or break UI/API representations of permissions referencing groups."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java",
      "line": 103,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No coverage for user count/query filtering driven by getGroupIdsWithViewPermission",
      "body": "The tests verify user search after granting group `view-members`, but they do not verify `/users/count` or paginated query behavior that relies on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. Because the V2 implementation of that method is broken for group resources, the missing coverage allows incorrect count/query filtering to pass. Add tests for user counts and paginated search with group member permissions."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Global group manage check grants manage for VIEW permission
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns true when the caller has either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). The no-argument `canManage()` is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` through `requireManage()`. A scope permission granting only `view` on `Groups` therefore allows creating or moving top-level groups, which is a privilege escalation. The check should require only `MANAGE`.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is used to populate `UserModel.GROUPS` for user queries and counts. In V2, group instance resources are named by the realm group ID (`AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` returns `group.getId()`), but this method adds `groupResource.getId()` (the internal authorization resource ID) and also passes that value to `hasPermission()`, which expects a group ID and looks the resource up by name. The returned set therefore does not contain realm group IDs, so user search/count filtering by group permissions is wrong. It should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the returned set.

findings.title: Instance resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` creates instance resources for `Clients`, `Groups`, and `Users` but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` relies on `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` to find group instance resources. If instance resources have no type, they will not be returned, so group-scoped `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are not translated into group IDs for user queries/counts. The created resource should have its type set to `resourceType`.

findings.title: Type-level group member permissions are not handled in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` scans all resources of type `Groups`, which includes the type-level resource named `Groups` representing all groups. If a permission grants `view-members`/`manage-members` on all groups, this method either adds the type resource identifier (currently the wrong ID, but even with `getName()` it would be the literal string `Groups`) or cannot represent the grant as a set of group IDs. User count/search APIs that use this set will not reflect all-groups member permissions. The method needs explicit handling for the type-level resource.

findings.title: Unsupported operations are thrown from V2 group permission management while existing code still calls them
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled()` (and `isPermissionsEnabled()`) throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. However `AdminPermissions.registerListener()` calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` on `GroupRemovedEvent` when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, and `GroupResource` management/permissions endpoints call `isPermissionsEnabled`/`setPermissionsEnabled`. If V1 and V2 fine-grained authz features are both enabled, group deletion or these endpoints can fail with an exception/500. For V2, cleanup/disable should be a no-op or the endpoints/listener must be guarded; throwing from lifecycle event handling is unsafe.

findings.title: Group-based user creation only checks V1 fine-grained authz feature
findings.body: `UsersResource.canCreateGroupMembers()` returns false unless `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. This PR implements V2 fine-grained authz group scopes (`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`), and `AdminPermissions.evaluator()` may use V2 even when the V1 feature is disabled. In that configuration, callers with V2 `manage-members`/`manage-membership` group permissions cannot create users with initial group membership because the fallback permission check is skipped. The check should also consider V2/admin permissions enabled.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException in getScope for missing/unknown resource type
findings.body: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope()`, when the authorization schema is supported, the code calls `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes()` without checking whether `resourceType` is null or present in the map. An invalid or missing resource type will cause an NPE and HTTP 500 instead of a validation error. It should validate `resourceType` and throw a `ModelValidationException`.

findings.title: Fallback to all-groups resource can NPE when type resource is unavailable
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can return null if the realm does not support the schema or the type resource has not been initialized. The method should null-check the fallback resource and return false instead of throwing NPE.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName()` special-cases only `USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. For `Groups`, instance resources are stored with the group ID as the name and no display name is set, so this method returns `resource.getDisplayName()` (likely null) or the raw ID instead of a useful group name/path, and it does not return a label for the all-groups type resource. This can degrade or break UI/API representations of permissions referencing groups.

findings.title: No coverage for user count/query filtering driven by getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
findings.body: The tests verify user search after granting group `view-members`, but they do not verify `/users/count` or paginated query behavior that relies on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. Because the V2 implementation of that method is broken for group resources, the missing coverage allows incorrect count/query filtering to pass. Add tests for user counts and paginated search with group member permissions.
